stem: Which clinical sign is specifically mentioned as a warning for a potential mandibular fracture following chinpoint trauma?

options.text: Exposed marrow on the maxillary incisors.
A laceration on the palate from a toothbrush.
Hemorrhage specifically from the gingival tissues of the upper teeth.

explanation: Bleeding under the tongue (sublingual hematoma) is a classic indicator that the jawbone may be fractured, particularly at the symphysis.
rationale: Look for a specific type of internal bruising in the floor of the mouth.

optionExplanations.A: Bleeding under the tongue (sublingual hematoma) is a classic indicator that the jawbone may be fractured, particularly at the symphysis.
optionExplanations.B: Exposed marrow indicates a crown fracture of the teeth, not necessarily a fracture of the mandible.
optionExplanations.C: Palatal lacerations are usually soft-tissue injuries resulting from falling with an object in the mouth, not jaw fractures.
optionExplanations.D: While upper gingival hemorrhage is common in dental trauma, it is not a specific hallmark of a mandibular (lower jaw) fracture.

source.hint: Look for a specific type of internal bruising in the floor of the mouth.
